_comment: Every callsite under cli/** that can put a body on the wire, enumerated by bin/uplink-guard.py.
This is not a list of the uplinks somebody remembered: the guard lexes the code, finds every
body-capable callsite, and requires each one to be claimed by EXACTLY ONE row here — so an
undeclared send reddens CI, a row whose callsite is gone reddens it, and a row pointed at some
harmless line reddens it too. `callsite` is the code text of the line the row accounts for and
must be unique within its file. kind=json is an uplink (route + OpenAPI $ref + the wire test that
compares ITS body); kind=seam is a shared send implementation uplinks travel through; kind=skip is
reachable but out of scope, with the reason committed rather than left as a silent pass.
NOTE on codex-context / codex-tokens: one producer call (reportTokenUsage) emits both, so they
share a subtest. Their wire_needle values differ because each names a distinct line of that
subtest — both bodies ARE compared, the loop walks every captured request.

the dispatch handler handed over as a VALUE: the stream calls it for every frame, and the sends below it are the frame handlers' own (member refetch, chat/reply-card/task drains). Taking the value is the callsite here — the call itself is spelled onData(…) inside the stream loop, a name no rule can know. It used to name the presence POST as what hangs below; that retired with the client-side stop reports (T-a9d6).
